title: Release audit: install.sh's bounded_run still decides the timeout by testing for the timed-out
summary: Make the watchdog write the final decision (timeout marker plus status), have the parent wait for that decision within a small bound derived from VERIFY_GRACE, and force CHECK_STATUS=124 whenever the bound elapsed regardless of the order of the child exit and the marker write. Add and commit the test whose checked shell exits just after FORGEL_CODE_TIMEOUT and assert install.sh fails with a message naming the limit.
requirements: When a verification command does not finish within its time limit, the installer must fail the installation and its failure must state that the time limit was exceeded.
That failure must occur regardless of whether the command ends just before, at, or just after the moment the limit elapses.
A verification command that finishes within its limit and reports success must let the installation continue.
A verification command that finishes within its limit and reports failure must be reported as that failure and must not be presented as a time-limit failure.
No situation may exist in which the installation is reported as successful for a verification run that exceeded its limit.
The installer's additional waiting for the outcome of a verification run after the limit has passed must be finite and short.
The verification step must leave no residual processes and no temporary working artifacts behind, including when the limit is exceeded.
The project's test suite must contain a regression test whose verification command ends just after the limit and which asserts that the installation fails with a message naming the limit.
The behavior of the installer for verification commands that finish well within their limit must remain unchanged.
All project artifacts are in English.
acceptance: A verification command that ends just after the time limit makes the installation fail with a message naming the time limit.
A verification command that succeeds well within the time limit lets the installation complete.
A verification command that fails with its own error within the time limit produces that error and not a time-limit message.
No run in which the time limit elapsed is reported as a successful installation.
The regression test for the just-after-limit case exists and passes, and the full test suite passes.
The pre-existing tests for within-limit verification pass without being weakened, showing that behavior for those cases is unchanged.
After an exceeded-limit run, no verification processes remain and no temporary working artifacts are left behind.
Every artifact produced is in English.
constraints: One change that a single agent can finish and verify on its own.
The time limit and its default value stay as they are.
No existing test may be weakened to make the new behavior pass.
Project and repository instructions and recorded user decisions are binding.
A verification command running past its limit must continue to fail the installation; only the correctness of that verdict changes.
plan_goal: Fix install.sh so a new terminal finds forgel-code on PATH

checks.criterion: A verification command that ends just after the time limit makes the installation fail with a message naming the time limit.
A verification command that succeeds well within the time limit lets the installation complete, and one that fails within the limit is not reported as a time limit.
After an exceeded-limit run, no verification processes remain and no temporary working artifacts are left behind.
The regression test for the just-after-limit case exists and passes, and the full test suite passes without weakened tests.
Behavior for within-limit verification is unchanged and all artifacts are in English.

external_dependencies.name: POSIX shell runtime of the environment where the installer runs
external_dependencies.interface: The installer and its tests run verification commands as child processes under a time limit; no new dependency is introduced.

result.summary: Fixed install.sh so the bounded verification check reports a time-limit failure whenever the check's own measured duration reaches the configured limit, instead of inferring the verdict solely from the watchdog's recorded marker. bounded_run now takes a timestamp with a new now_millis helper before starting the check and again when the check's result is available; the verdict is 124 when the elapsed time reaches limit*1000 milliseconds or when the watchdog recorded 'timed-out'. The wait for the watchdog's record stays bounded by DECISION_WAIT, the existing graceful/forceful stop and cleanup paths are unchanged (so no residual processes or private directories remain), and the time limit, its default and all user-facing message wording are untouched. Added tests/test_install_timeout_verdict.py, which drives the real installer through tests/test_install helpers with a deterministic 'date' stub (a fabricated clock) and asserts: just-after-limit, at-limit and early-exit-before-marker runs all fail with 'the check was stopped after 1s' and leave no check directory behind, while an in-limit run keeps its own nonzero status and is not reported as a timeout. Verified with `sh -n install.sh` and the full suite: `python -m pytest -q` -> 218 passed, 137 subtests passed.
assumptions: The check's duration is measured from just before the command is started to just after its own status is available, and duration >= limit counts as exceeding the limit (the limit is inclusive, matching 'ends just before, at, or just after').
When no usable clock is available (the helper reports 0), the watchdog's recorded 'timed-out' marker remains the fallback verdict, as before.
The regression test forces the just-after-limit case deterministically with a stubbed clock rather than relying on real process timing, so it cannot be flaky.
Existing exit cleanup (stop_check plus removal of the private check directory) already satisfies the no-residual-processes/artifacts requirement and was left unchanged.
